scenarios.title: The Charity Basketball Game
scenarios.text: A charity basketball game with teammates in a high school gym, and you are, by a wide margin, the worst player on the court. The crowd has noticed.

choices.label: Play it for laughs
choices.result: Every miss, celebrated like a championship. The crowd loves it, the clips go around, and the charity raises more than it ever has.

choices.label: Practice for a week
choices.result: A week of secret practice in your driveway. You score twice in the game, and your teammates are genuinely amazed.

choices.label: Coach from the bench
choices.result: A clipboard, a whistle and the bench. You coach your team to a win, and the losing team demands a rematch.

scenarios.title: Supporting a Teammate's Cause
scenarios.text: A teammate is launching a foundation for kids in his old neighborhood and asks you to stand beside him. It's his cause, and he's nervous about it.

choices.label: Show up
choices.result: Every event this season, and you show up early to each one. He stops looking nervous by the third, and you help him with the speeches.

choices.label: Help with the plan
choices.result: You help him build the plan, not just the photos: a budget, a board, a calendar. A year later, it's still running.

choices.label: Donate quietly
choices.result: A quiet donation and your best wishes. He's grateful, and you can tell from his face that he hoped you'd stand beside him.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival on Your Team
scenarios.text: A kicker you competed with all through college signs with your club as a backup. He beat you for a scholarship once. Now he's the one on the practice squad.

choices.label: Bury the old rivalry
choices.result: Lunch on his first day, and the old rivalry turns into a joke you both share. By midseason, he's your best friend on the team.

choices.label: Stay ahead every day
choices.result: Ahead of him every day, by a little. He notices, you notice, and neither of you says a word about the scholarship.

choices.label: Help him fit in
choices.result: His introduction to the room, made by you, generously. The room notices how you handle it, and so does {coach}, who says nothing and remembers.

scenarios.title: The Brother's Wedding
scenarios.text: {sibling} is getting married on a game weekend. The date was set before the schedule came out, and {sibling} has already asked you to give the toast.

choices.label: Fly in for the wedding
choices.result: The Friday, granted by {coach}, a flight back Saturday night. You give the toast, and {sibling} doesn't stop crying through it.

choices.label: Help move the date
choices.result: A different date, found together with {sibling}, who moves it a week. You're there all weekend, and so is the rest of the family.

choices.label: Send a video toast
choices.result: A video toast, recorded in the locker room. {sibling} plays it twice, and you watch the reception on a phone in a hotel.

scenarios.title: The City Starts to Feel Like Home
scenarios.text: One morning you realize you know your neighbors' names, your barista knows your order, and the dry cleaner asks about your knee. The city has started to feel like home.

choices.label: Put down roots
choices.result: A neighborhood group, a library card, a farmers' market on Saturdays. You start saying yes to things, and the city says yes back.

choices.label: Enjoy it quietly
choices.result: Quietly, you enjoy it. Home is a nice word, and you don't need to say it out loud to anyone to feel it.

choices.label: Think about staying for good
choices.result: A question you've never asked: what if you stayed here after football? You start reading about schools and neighborhoods at night.

scenarios.title: The Sponsor's Event
scenarios.text: Your sponsor wants you at a store opening on your only day off this month. It's three hours away, there's a ribbon to cut, and the regional manager has already announced you.

choices.label: Go and do it well
choices.result: You go, cut the ribbon, sign for two hours and smile until your face hurts. The sponsor is thrilled, and your day off disappears.

choices.label: Offer another day
choices.result: A different day, offered politely. They take it, and reschedule the ribbon, and the regional manager pretends it was his idea.

choices.label: Keep your day off
choices.result: No, politely, and you keep your day off. The sponsor is a little cooler next time, and you sleep until ten.

scenarios.title: The Mid-Career Check-In
scenarios.text: Your agent takes you to lunch and asks a question nobody's asked you before: where do you want to be in five years? Not the contract. The life.

choices.label: Write it down
choices.result: The club, the house, the people, the life after, written on a napkin. Your agent keeps the napkin and brings it to every meeting.

choices.label: Aim for the top
choices.result: The top, you say: the best in the league, the biggest contract, the Hall of Fame. Your agent smiles and gets to work.

choices.label: Ask your family first
choices.result: Your family first, you say, and you ask them that night. Their answer surprises you, and it changes the next contract.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Gets Rich
scenarios.text: A teammate signs a huge contract and starts acting like it: the new watch, the entourage, the late arrivals, a new way of talking to the equipment staff.

choices.label: Talk to him as a friend
choices.result: A quiet word, as a friend, in the parking lot. He hears it, eventually, and apologizes to the equipment staff on his own.

choices.label: Keep the room together
choices.result: The room, kept from turning on him. You defend him in public and push him in private, and by December he's himself again.

choices.label: Let him be
choices.result: Money changes people for a while, you decide, and you let him be. He comes back to earth by spring, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Practice Squad Kicker
scenarios.text: The practice squad kicker is good, really good, and the coaches know it. They've started watching his kicks as closely as yours, and he's started noticing.

choices.label: Raise your level
choices.result: Your level, raised, and kept there. Every practice is better than the last, and the coaches start watching your kicks again.

choices.label: Help him anyway
choices.result: Help, freely given: his plant foot, his routine, his nerves. He'll get a job somewhere, and he'll remember who helped him.

choices.label: Ask where you stand
choices.result: {coach}, asked plainly where you stand. The answer is fair and a little uncomfortable, and you leave with a clear target.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Net in the Living Room
scenarios.text: You set up a kicking net in the living room for winter practice, right in front of the television. {love_interest} has opinions, mostly about the lamp that's already broken.

choices.label: Move it to the garage
choices.result: The net, moved to the garage, with a space heater. Peace returns to the house, the lamp is replaced, and the garage becomes your favorite room.

choices.label: Negotiate a deal
choices.result: A deal: weekdays only, and you hang the paintings that have been leaning on the wall since you moved in. Everyone wins.

choices.label: Keep the net
choices.result: The net stays where it is. Some arguments are worth having, you decide, and you kick very carefully around the brand-new lamp all winter.

scenarios.title: The Season-Ticket Holder
scenarios.text: A season-ticket holder has sat in the same seat behind the bench for thirty years, and talks to you every single week: weather, wind, his late wife's opinions on kickers.

choices.label: Learn his story
choices.result: His story, over a dozen conversations: he was here for every era of this club, good and terrible. You start looking for him before warmups.

choices.label: Bring him onto the field
choices.result: A practice pass, arranged by you. He walks onto the field for the first time in thirty years and has to sit down.

choices.label: Wave every week
choices.result: A wave every week, and he waves back from his seat. It's small and steady, and you'd miss it terribly if it ever stopped.

scenarios.title: The Charity Visit You Remember
scenarios.text: A charity visit to the children's hospital leaves a mark. One kid, eight years old, asked you to kick a paper ball across his room, and you can't stop thinking about him.

choices.label: Go back on your own
choices.result: Back, on your own, without cameras, twice a month. The kid's family remembers you forever, and you remember them every time you see a paper ball.

choices.label: Start something
choices.result: A small fund for the hospital, started by you and run by a nurse. It buys games, tablets and paper balls, and it's still running years later.

choices.label: Keep his drawing in your locker
choices.result: His drawing of you, kicking a paper ball, goes in your locker. You look at it before every game, and it calms you more than any routine.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Staff Dinner
scenarios.text: The coaches invite you to dinner at the head coach's house, which they've never done before. You're the only player there, and there are place cards.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: Dinner, stories and a long evening on the patio. They're people too, it turns out, and the head coach does a very bad impression of you.

choices.label: Go and listen closely
choices.result: Mostly listening, all evening. You learn what they think of the special teams, and what they think of you, and both are useful.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: A polite no. It feels strange to eat with the people who decide your job, and you're not sure that's a good reason.
